_client_secret: Needed to stay logged in. Twitch only lets a Public client refresh without one; the console defaults to Confidential. Leave it out and the bot must be re-authorised about every 4 hours.
_fact_source: 'sources' (default): find real facts on Wikipedia/web, then rewrite them. 'llm': skip retrieval and ask the model for facts from its own knowledge - simpler and often better for famous places, but nothing is verified, so it can invent.
_tavily_api_key: Optional. tavily.com: 1,000 free searches a month, no card. Used for free-form question sources and, with topic 'news', for what-happened questions ('who got into a helicopter crash today in California'). Without it, news questions use Google News' keyless RSS search - still real headlines with outlet and age, just no key required. Either way a news question is answered with the headline itself, never a model's guess and never an encyclopedia line.
_news_country: Whose front page 'docbot whats the headlines today' reads: a two-letter country code for Google News' top-stories edition (US, GB, AU, CA...). A headline ask with no subject ('whats the news', 'top stories', 'whats going on in the world') is answered from that edition's top stories - three real story titles per message, each with outlet and age, and a repeat of the ask rotates to the next three. Roundup page titles ('Top news of the day September 16 2026') are never quoted as headlines. Asks WITH a subject ('news on the LA bus crash') still search for that subject.
_weatherapi_key: Free key from weatherapi.com/signup (1M calls/month). When set, a weather question is answered from weatherapi.com as ONE sentence to the asker: 'kvack, it is currently Clear in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania. 63°F (17°C). Feels like 61°F (16°C). Wind is blowing from the SW at 4 mph (7 km/h). 61% humidity. Visibility: 6 miles (10 km). Precipitation: 0.0 in (0.0 mm).' Works for a mention ('docbot weather in scranton?') and !ask alike; answers are cached 5 minutes per place. Left empty (or if the key is rejected / the place is unknown / the service is down) the keyless Open-Meteo path answers instead, headed 'Weather | place: ...'. The WEATHERAPI_KEY environment variable also works.
_llm_options: The three llm_* fields above are set for OpenRouter (recommended for adult-aligned facts). Other providers: Groq -> key 'gsk_...', base 'https://api.groq.com/openai/v1', model 'openai/gpt-oss-120b'. Local Ollama -> key '' (empty), base 'http://localhost:11434/v1', model 'llama3.1:8b'. Other OpenRouter models: 'sao10k/l3.3-euryale-70b' (edgiest), 'cognitivecomputations/dolphin-mistral-24b-venice-edition' (uncensored), 'mistralai/mistral-nemo' (cheapest).
_llm_fallback_providers: Optional ORDERED LIST of second providers, each with its own key and its own rest window, tried in this order until one answers - so one dead key is skipped instead of taking the rest down. Entries look like {"base_url": "https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1", "key_env": "NVIDIA_API_KEY", "model": "openai/gpt-oss-120b, nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b"} (or put the key inline as "key", though key_env keeps it in bot.env where the admin panel never writes it). The trio above still works and is always tried first, so an existing config needs no change. A key already in the environment adds its provider by itself - NVIDIA_API_KEY brings NVIDIA NIM (https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1, free developer key, ~40 requests a minute shared across every model, hosts the same gpt-oss models Groq does) and GEMINI_API_KEY brings Google AI Studio (https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai, free per-project quota; gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-3.5-flash-lite are the current picks - Gemini 3.x always thinks, and the bot sends it the reasoning budget it needs, so leave llm_no_think off for it). Startup prints one 'fallback READY' line per provider in the order they are tried; the admin panel's System tab shows the chain and which one is resting.
_llm_fallback: The bot's second LLM provider: when the llm_* provider above is rate-limited (Groq's free tier 429s mid-stream), chat replies, sourced answers and fact writing switch to this provider until the window clears, and both are warmed at startup. FREE OpenRouter setup: key 'sk-or-...' (create one at openrouter.ai/keys, no card needed), base 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1' (the default when left empty), model a slug ending in ':free' - or a COMMA-SEPARATED CHAIN of them, tried in order, e.g. 'nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free, nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free, cohere/north-mini-code:free' (Sept 2026: all three answer in about a second; the 550b nemotron 'ultra' takes 20-30 s a line). Rate limits are per MODEL: a 429 rests only that model, for as long as the error says (a Groq 'tokens per day' message rests it until the quoted reset), and the line moves on - on Groq to openai/gpt-oss-20b's separate budget first (Groq retired the Llama 3.x slugs in Aug 2026; a config naming one is told at startup), then down this chain. The bot uses exactly the models you list: it never substitutes the random openrouter/free router and never adds a paid model to the second-provider path. OpenRouter allows 50 free requests/day on an account that never bought credits and 1,000/day after a one-time $10 purchase; free slugs rotate monthly and shared capacity can fill, so recheck openrouter.ai/models when warm-up says fallback NOT READY. A local Ollama fallback also works: key '', base 'http://localhost:11434/v1', model 'qwen3:4b' - no key, no limits, no rotation. Leave llm_fallback_model empty (the default) to keep a single provider. Startup first prints fallback READY, OFF or MISCONFIGURED for the config, then the live warm-up prints fallback READY only after an answer or fallback NOT READY with the provider's real error.
_moderation: Moderation on request: a moderator can tell the bot what to do - '!ban <name> [reason]', '!timeout <name> [10m] [reason]', '!unban <name>' - in chat or in a private message. In chat the badges decide, and Twitch's LEAD MODERATOR role counts (it replaces the moderator badge, so a bot that only looks for 'moderator' ignores it). A private message carries no channel badges, so mod_logins is who may ask that way: a list of Twitch logins, e.g. ["hiswife", "leadmod1"]; the broadcaster and the bot itself are always allowed. The bot will not ban the broadcaster, itself, or anyone on this list. Needs the bot to be a moderator of the channel AND the moderator:manage:banned_users scope in its login: run 'python3 bot.py --login' once after upgrading ('--doctor' lists the scopes the stored token has). Twitch switched the IRC /ban commands off on 18 Feb 2023, so this is the Helix API - and whispers arrive over EventSub, not IRC, so a private ask is best-effort while the in-chat command always works. mod_timeout_seconds is the default length for !timeout with no length given (30s / 10m / 2h / 1d also work). Set mod_commands_enabled false to switch the lot off.
_chat_ai: The bot's own voice in chat. When enabled: !ask anything gets a persona answer (needs the llm_* fields; without a key, !ask falls back to the fact engine), and the bot replies when addressed by one of chat_ai_names. Autonomous chimes are rare and only happen in light conversation; once chat_ai_busy_messages arrive inside chat_ai_busy_seconds the bot listens unless asked. A quiet-room opener can happen after chat_ai_quiet_seconds, but only once per human conversation lull - it never repeats on a timer into silence. chat_ai_chance is the odds per eligible light-chat moment, chat_ai_cooldown separates autonomous attempts, chat_ai_max_hour caps autonomous posts, and !cb off silences them. bot_personality empty = the built-in Doc voice.
_chat_ai_ack: When a question is held by a rail - the asker's own chat_ai_mention_cooldown, the channel pace, or the hourly cap - the bot is still going to answer it, but until then the room sees nothing, and from chat a rail and a crash look exactly the same. That silence is why the same question gets asked three times. With chat_ai_ack_held the bot says so at once, quoting the wait: '@marblehead9 on it - give me about 45 seconds to look that up.' One promise per person (a repeat ask inside the window gets no second 'on it'), nothing below chat_ai_ack_min_seconds (the answer is seconds away, so a message about it would be noise), and if a held question is lost - the queue filled, or it went stale - the asker is told to ask again rather than left thinking they were ignored. Set chat_ai_ack_held false for the old silence.
_chat_ai_mention: chat_ai_mention_cooldown is PER VIEWER: one persona reply per person per 60 s, so nobody winds the bot up like a toy - but Dani's question is never held behind Yeyeboi's minute. chat_ai_mention_pace is the channel-wide floor between any two persona replies. A question inside the asker's own cooldown is held (one per person, eight people deep) and answered to them when their clock clears; every hold or drop is a log line.
_chat_ai_distill: How often the memory distill (a second model call that turns a viewer's recent lines into remembered facts) may run per viewer: on first contact, then only after chat_ai_distill_minutes AND chat_ai_distill_lines new lines from them. It used to run after every reply and ate ~40% of the daily token budget.
_chat_ai_names: Words that address the bot in chat and get a reply. The bot's own nick (the "nick" field above) is ALWAYS a trigger too, automatically - with nick "TruckingWithDocBot", typing TruckingWithDocBot, doc or docbot all work. Matching is on word boundaries and case-insensitive, so 'doc' does not fire inside 'dockyard'.
_memory_db: The chat AI's memory (one SQLite file). While chat_ai_enabled is true, chat is logged (pruned after 90 days) and the bot distills durable per-viewer facts after it talks - work, pets, hobbies, plans, preferences. Health, politics, religion, finances and anything intimate are never kept. A moderator can erase a viewer entirely with !forget <viewer>.
_chat_ai_perform_delay: Seconds between the lines when the chat AI performs - 'docbot sing me a song', 'make me a poem', 'tell us a story', a rap, a limerick, a haiku, a toast. The piece is written whole, checked line by line, and posted one line at a time so it reads like a delivery, not a wall. Empty = the same gap as beef_act_delay; 0 posts the whole piece at once.
_chat_ai_notice_minutes: How long a mod's announcement stands as the bot's answer to a confused room. 'Docbot tell everyone that @Doc is on the phone, radio silence' (mods and the broadcaster only) is answered in character as before AND kept as a standing notice: for this many minutes anyone who sounds lost about the quiet stream - 'your mic is muted', 'hello?', 'can't hear you', 'is he afk?', addressed to the bot or not - gets '@name heads up: Doc is on the phone, radio silence' once each, with no chime roll and no cooldown, and the persona sees the notice in its prompt. 'Docbot tell everyone doc is back' clears it early. 0 turns the feature off.
_llm_no_think: Set true when llm_model is a Qwen3-family model running locally (qwen3:8b, qwen3:4b): appends Qwen3's /no_think switch to every prompt so the model answers directly instead of thinking first - on CPU, thinking turns a one-line chat reply into a half-minute stall.
_admin_panel: A password-protected web page served by the bot itself: dashboard (connected, AI provider and rate-limit rests, Twitch login health), live log, pause/resume and the !so/!cb/!beef switches, speak as the bot, standing notice, reminders, custom commands, haul, sub goal, voice, viewer memory, a config.json editor with masked secrets, panel users, Twitch re-login and a Restart button. Setup: python3 bot.py --admin-user yourname (prompts for a password; add --role mod for a moderator login that gets the switches but not config/secrets/restart), then set admin_panel_enabled true and restart. It listens on admin_panel_bind:admin_panel_port - 127.0.0.1 by default, so on a server reach it over an SSH tunnel (ssh -L 8477:127.0.0.1:8477 user@server, then http://localhost:8477) or set admin_panel_bind to the machine's Tailscale 100.x address so only your own devices can see it. 0.0.0.0 or a public IP is refused unless admin_panel_public is true too; only do that behind HTTPS (Caddy, nginx) and a firewall. Logins are salted PBKDF2 hashes in admin_users.json (gitignored), sessions are HttpOnly cookies that expire after 12 idle hours, 5 wrong passwords lock the name for 15 minutes, and every action is written to the bot's log as [admin].
_log_file: Set to a filename (e.g. "bot.log") and everything the console shows is also appended to that file - including crash tracebacks - so the log survives the window scrolling away. Watch it live with PowerShell: Get-Content .\bot.log -Wait. Empty = console only.
_persona_state_path: Where the mod-chosen voice (!persona set) is saved so it survives restarts. The bot's available voices: doc, sarge, rookie, rusty, nightshift, medic, cb, squaddie, coach, cowboy, flo, commentator, noir (or !persona custom <description>) - and whichever is active, it always knows the streamer's story.
_ongoing: The chat AI's working memory - what it is in the middle of, as opposed to what it remembers about people. A mod or the streamer can have it host a quiz in plain chat ('docbot lets do a test run, topic cycling, 3 rounds' / 'start the first round' / 'round 2, give 30 secs to answer then start round 3 30 secs after that' / 'whats the answer' / 'game over'): it asks one real question per round, keeps the round open until the host calls time (or the timing he asked for runs out), gives the answer, refuses lookups of the open question, and knows in every reply that it is hosting and where it is up to. And it keeps counts ('keep count of dirty lepages' / 'dirty lepage!' / '+1' / 'how many so far?' / 'scratch that' / 'stop counting'): arithmetic the bot does itself, no model, exact an hour later. Both are saved in ongoing_state_path so a restart mid-game is not amnesia. A game untouched for chat_ai_activity_minutes is dropped; counts stay until stopped. chat_ai_count_anyone true lets any viewer bump a count (off: the mods, the streamer and whoever opened it - anyone can always ASK for it).
_subgoal_state_path: Where the sub goal (!subgoal set <goal> <what happens when we hit it>) is saved. Twitch only lets the broadcaster's own token read live sub counts, so mods keep the number moving with !subgoal add/sub/count - anyone can check it with a bare !subgoal.
_subgoal_auto_count: true (the default): every sub, resub and gifted sub the bot SEES announced in chat bumps the sub goal on its own - the community-gift banner is skipped so gifts are never counted twice, and crossing the goal posts the payoff line. Anything the bot misses while offline is corrected with !subgoal count N. false: mods move the number entirely by hand.
